title: FOMC minutes (June 8-9 2027 meeting) — the first minutes release in 20 years to land on a quarter's final session
source: EST: federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, re-fetched direct 2026-09-06 by this lane (HTTP 200, 164,826 bytes) and re-parsed rather than inherited. It states the convention verbatim -- "The minutes of regularly scheduled meetings are released three weeks after the date of the policy decision" -- and its 2027 panel reads verbatim "January 26-27 | March 16-17* | April 27-28 | June 8-9* | July 27-28 | September 14-15* | October 26-27 | December 7-8*" with "* Meeting associated with a Summary of Economic Projections.", so the decision day 2027-06-09 plus 21 days is Wednesday 2027-06-30 (weekday verified, not assumed). THE RULE IS MEASURED ACROSS TWENTY YEARS, NOT FIVE: this session parsed the Released dates off fomccalendars.htm AND off the fourteen fomchistorical<year>.htm pages 2007-2020 (all HTTP 200), giving 160 distinct minutes release dates 2007-02-21 through 2026-08-19, every one of which is a trading session. The proposal that seeded this entry measured 42 of 45 at exactly 21 days on the 2021-2026 panel alone; the wider set carries the same rule with the same class of exception (holiday-shifted releases in late Nov/Dec). The rule also reproduces every fomc-minutes entry this calendar already tracks (2026-09-16 -> 2026-10-07, 2026-10-28 -> 2026-11-18, 2026-12-09 -> 2026-12-30). STATUS STAYS ESTIMATE for the same reason every 2027 entry here does, and not for want of a primary: the same page states verbatim "Each meeting date is tentative until confirmed at the meeting immediately preceding it", so the promotion trigger is the 2027-04-27/28 meeting ratifying the June date, not a better fetch. federalreserve.gov/newsevents/2027-june.htm and /2027-july.htm both returned 404 to this session -- the month pages that carry the 2:00 p.m. release time do not exist yet -- and are recorded in the ledger's probe-ref blocked array. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: CANONICAL FILE written by the fomc-minutes-2027-06-30 initial-research lane (2026-09-06) after reading the one prior proposal, proposals/fomc-minutes-2027-06-30.from-consumer-confidence-2027-06-29.json, which is now inert. THE FINDING THAT EARNS THE ENTRY IS NOT THE PAIRING THE PROPOSAL NAMED. Measured on all 160 minutes releases 2007-2026: NONE has ever landed on a quarter's final trading session (closest ever: 2025-12-30 at one session before year end, and 2020-07-01 at one session after quarter end), and all twenty June-meeting minutes published in JULY, the earliest ever being 2020-07-01. 2027-06-30 would be the first FOMC minutes release in the record to publish on a quarter-end session and the first June-meeting minutes to publish inside June at all. The cause is mechanical and already measured next door: fomc-2027-06-09's ledger found every 2027 FOMC sits one day earlier than its 2026 counterpart EXCEPT June, which sits eight days earlier, making 2027-06-09 the earliest June FOMC in the 21-year record -- that eight-day shift is exactly what drags the minutes out of July and onto the quarter's last close. THE CHANNEL CLAIM THE FAMILY CARRIES IS CORRECTED, NOT REPEATED. The three sibling ledgers argued 'read it, do not trade it' from n=3 all inside +/-0.3%. At n=160 that sample is unrepresentative: minutes-day |S&P| runs 0.776% mean / 0.468% median against a 0.798% / 0.523% unconditional 2007-2026 baseline (bootstrap p=0.40), 33.1% of minutes days close within +/-0.3% against 33.4% of all sessions, and 20 of 160 moved at least 1.5% (2008-11-19 -6.12%, 2008-10-07 -5.74%, 2025-04-09 +9.52%) against a 14.1% baseline rate. The honest statement is that a minutes day is an ORDINARY session carrying a full session's tail -- none of it attributable to the minutes -- not a quiet one. THE VENUE ARGUMENT IS ALSO CORRECTED: fomc-minutes-2026-12-30 leaned on thin dead-week tape as 'the most amplification-friendly venue a minutes release ever gets'. Measured against trailing-60d median volume, the dead week (Dec 28-31) runs 0.676x while June quarter-end runs 1.149x against a 1.027x all-session mean, so the genuinely amplification-friendly venue is the quarter-end close, and 2027-06-30 is a STRONGER test of the same null rather than a weaker one. THE PROPOSAL'S PAIRING CLAIM IS TRUE OF THIS CALENDAR BUT NOT STRUCTURALLY NOVEL: a minutes release landing the session after a Conference Board last-Tuesday print has four precedents in twenty years (2007-05-30 +0.80%, 2020-07-01 +0.50%, 2020-11-25 -0.16%, 2025-05-28 -0.56%) -- every one inside +/-0.8%. ONE ADJACENCY PROPOSED, on this event's own date: sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2027-06-30 (estimate), the June analogue of the March entry, whose rule this session re-fetched verbatim from SEC EDGAR rather than inheriting. RUSSELL RECONSTITUTION IS REFUSED, not forgotten: ftserussell.com/resources/russell-reconstitution (HTTP 200) publishes no 2027 calendar and states no dating rule, so a 2027-06-25 estimate would be a rule-derived date on an unstated rule; it is carried as a dated watch item in the ledger instead. Estimate widens caution only and licenses nothing; symbols is empty and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed.
